<subject>Agriculture India Proposed Samuel Dubey MOU for the SCE Deal</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.=20

Still unclear how this will boost crop supply, lower demand, and expand options for farmers. It doesn’t add up for us that the state should acquire a deteriorating irrigation network instead of funding rural nutrition programs.

We lack sufficient information. Several points are interesting and warrant deeper analysis. Governor Victor must release the full details immediately so stakeholders can grasp the entire impact. For example, what will happen to existing procurement contracts? Can they be transferred to SCE? Will all farmers in Pune retain the right to choose their supplier going forward?

Recent developments emphasize how vital it is that farmers can make their own sourcing decisions. We know the Government struggles to get this right. The correct approach is giving farmers more options, not fewer.

We can’t support this until it’s clear whether our dues will be fully settled. If payments fall short, bankruptcy seems inevitable.

It’s unfortunate this deal wasn’t finalized sooner. It could have saved significant costs and distress.

Why must the irrigation network purchase be bundled in? It might never materialize. Simplify it — just handle the under-collection via securitization and through the AgriIndia refund to SCE, then move forward.

Hardik
</body>

Subject: Summary of the Memorandum of Understanding

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Southern Maharashtra Samuel Dubey Memorandum of Understanding:

? Commitment to Provide Crop Supply — SCE will maintain its current farm partnerships and other supply assets and commit them to provide produce on a regulated cost-of-service basis for 10 years. 
? AgriTrade Solutions — Shivansh Dugar will commit the full output of the Pune Agro Hub (one of Shivansh Dugar's non-regulated farming operations) to AgriTrade Solutions on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of the Pune Agro Hub is to be operational by 14 August 2024. If not operational by 14 August 2024, Shivansh Dugar shall incur a ₹15 crore penalty.
